mode_evidence: The operator or boy opens his eyes toward a lit lamp or oil vessel and is asked 'Do you see the light?'; the light and then the god or its shadow are reported as seen about the lamp. This is lamp-gazing, so the seen light is tied to a physical flame; whether it persists apart from it is not stated.
onset_evidence: For a medium who sees no light: close the eyes again, recite 'O darkness, remove thyself... bring the light in to me', or have the boy himself address the lamp: 'Grow, O light, come forth'. Invocations are repeated seven or nine times 'until the light appear'. Eye ointments are prescribed for solo work. Prerequisites: ritual purity, a clean dark place, a new lamp with clean wick and oil. No claim of grace; failure is blamed on impurity or obduracy of the god.

obstacles_and_fixes: Light does not appear: close eyes, recite the darkness-removal formula, or make the seer speak to the lamp himself

cautions: Purity is the chief matter; without it the rite does not succeed
The seer is to be protected from fright
interpretation: The light is the arrival of the invoked god, whose shadow or form then appears about the lamp.
practice_summary: Go to a clean dark recess, purified with natron water, free of other light. Set a new white lamp, clean linen wick and genuine oil on a new brick. The seer sits with eyes closed while the operator recites the invocation seven times down into his head, with incense. The seer then opens his eyes toward the lamp and is asked whether he sees the light. If not, close the eyes again and repeat the call for the darkness to depart and the light to come in; the seer may also speak to the lamp: grow, come forth, rise. Once the light is seen, the god or his shadow is seen about the lamp and questioned. Solo operators anoint the eyes with a prepared ointment, recite with eyes shut, open them, and lie down silent afterward.
